Mr. President, I have the honor to inform the Council that Bangladesh, Egypt, Nepal, and other members of our core group intend to present during the 63rd session of the Human Rights Council a draft resolution under agenda item three entitled, Implications of Artificial Intelligence for the Promotion and Protection of Human Rights. Artificial intelligence is developing at an extraordinary pace and is increasingly becoming part of the way individuals, societies, governments and institutions function. Its applications are already transforming access to information, education, healthcare, scientific research, public services, and economic opportunities. We therefore approach artificial intelligence first and foremost with the recognition of its significant potential to contribute to the promotion and protection of human rights, sustainable development, and innovation. At the same time, the increasing use of AI, particularly where they influence or support decisions affecting individuals, also raises important human rights considerations. The proposed initiative, hence, seeks to provide a balanced, constructive and consensus oriented platform for the Council to consider these evolving issues specifically through the lens of international human rights law. Mr. President, We are fully mindful of the considerable work already undertaken within the United Nations system, including within this Council, on the human rights dimensions of technological changes. The proposed initiative is therefore not intended to duplicate existing processes or to create parallel mechanisms as such. Rather, our intention is to build upon existing work and provide a focused opportunity to consider how established human rights principles can remain meaningful and effective as artificial intelligence systems increasingly influence different aspects of people's lives. Moreover, We believe that international cooperation, capacity building, and meaningful participation must also form an integral part of our collective consideration of AI and human rights. Mr. President, Bangladesh, Egypt, Nepal, and other members of our core group are committed to conducting this initiative in an open, inclusive, and transparent manner. We look forward to consulting closely with all Member States and relevant stakeholders and to benefiting from their valuable views. Our objective is to work together towards a balanced and forward-looking text that can be adopted by consensus and enjoy the broadest possible support of the Council. I thank you, Mr. President.

Thank you, Mr. President. I would like to begin by thanking delegations for their constructive rationalization efforts so far this year. We have made good progress, and we encourage everyone to consider the information and tools shared by the co-facilitators when preparing their resolutions. Australia together with Timor-Leste will present the resolution on national human rights institutions at the 63rd session of the Human Rights Council. NHRIs are among the most important actors and independent voices for the promotion and protection of human rights. They bridge the gap between international human rights standards and implementation on the ground, empowering individuals to understand and exercise their human rights and contributing to the work of the Council, and the broader multilateral human rights system. Since being endorsed by the UN General Assembly in 1993, the Paris Principles have provided the international benchmark for the independent, pluralistic and effective NHRIs. Roughly three quarters of the current HRC membership have a national human rights institution, and we continue to see growing interest and progress globally in establishing and accrediting NHRIs. The resolution will continue to support the vital work of the Global Alliance of National Human Rights Institutions through the Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights to ensure a rigorous, fair, and inclusive accreditation process. At a time of increasing pressure on civic space, strong, independent and adequately resourced NHRIs are more important than ever. This is an important initiative to ensure that NHRIs remain independent, effective and equipped to respond to emerging human rights challenges. In this context, at this session, the resolution will focus on the role of NHRIs in promoting and protecting human rights in the digital space. NHRIs are well placed to monitor, assess and advise on the human rights implications of digital technologies, including artificial intelligence, to help prevent and mitigate harms and to support human rights based approaches. We will also move future iterations of the resolution to a triennial cycle, contributing to the collective effort to rationalize the workload of the council. We invite all delegations to engage constructively in the negotiations process and hope to reach a position that will allow the resolution to once again be adopted by the Council by consensus. I thank you.
